contract.hypothesis: Ground-field frozen-orbital Dirac-Fock/RCI supplies an independently defined free-ion baseline when five-level EOL orbital optimization fails its stationarity gate. Experiment tests this approximation separately.

fixed_conditions.Hamiltonian: finite-Fermi-nucleus Dirac-Coulomb on shared frozen Dirac-Fock orbitals
fixed_conditions.orbital_objective: native fac_frozen protocol: optimize first 4f14 6s configuration; four spectator orbitals have 0.001 initializer populations each, but all physical CI states contain exactly 69 electrons

contract.observable: resolved many-electron energy differences and finite-wavelength E1/E2/M1 tensors in the same common orbital basis
contract.distinguishing_outcomes: SCF/metric failure blocks production rates; radial drift >1 cm^-1 blocks a radial-convergence claim; experiment >5% fails the mean-field accuracy goal and motivates correlation/configuration expansion.
contract.resource_estimate: 5 CSFs, 5 one-dimensional J/parity blocks, 24 radial orbitals; spline matrices a few hundred squared; anticipated <3 GiB RSS. No 69-electron SD expansion requested.
contract.stopping_rule: 900 seconds per solve; stop on exception or unconverged orbital solution, retaining diagnostics; never change state weights or insert empirical offsets to pass.
contract.interpretation_limit: Ground-field SCF convergence and CI matrix convergence do not certify five-level EOL or frozen excited-orbital stationarity. The failed EOL results remain failed.
